facts: The paper addresses the problem of populating object category detection datasets with dense, per-object 3D reconstructions.
The dense, per-object 3D reconstructions are bootstrapped from class labels.
The dense, per-object 3D reconstructions are bootstrapped from ground truth figure-ground segmentations.
The dense, per-object 3D reconstructions are bootstrapped from a small set of keypoint annotations.
The proposed algorithm first estimates camera viewpoint using rigid structure-from-motion.
The proposed algorithm reconstructs object shapes by optimizing over visual hull proposals.
The optimization over visual hull proposals is guided by loose within-class shape similarity assumptions.
The visual hull sampling process attempts to intersect an object's projection cone with the cones of minimal subsets of other similar objects.
The similar objects considered by the visual hull sampling process are among those pictured from certain vantage points.
The method is able to produce convincing per-object 3D reconstructions on one of the most challenging existing object-category detection datasets, PASCAL VOC.
PASCAL VOC is one of the most challenging existing object-category detection datasets.
The results may re-stimulate once popular geometry-oriented model-based recognition approaches.
